criteria.cgo_official: Pin pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2: official tagged binding, ~5 ms cold invocations, ~12 MB peak batch RSS, 13461954-byte harness binary. Building canlc requires clang and CGO_ENABLED=1, changing the current CGO_ENABLED=0 launcher build; that toolchain is a documented developer prerequisite, not a user runtime dependency.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide the binding, or neither binding keeps the required contracts.
criteria.wasm_wazero: Pin go-pgquery v0.0.0-20260915022521-81f99195012b with wazero v1.12.0: pure-Go builds with no C toolchain and identical parse/scan outputs, at ~454 ms cold compile plus ~300 MB transient peak per SQL-touching process, a 20639362-byte binary, and an untagged third-party pin.

binding_choice.instructions: Choose the production SQL parser binding to pin: the official CGo binding or the WASM/wazero binding. Use common and topics.binding_choice.

criteria.closed_reasons: Map each failure to a small fixed reason set (for example syntax versus scanner versus empty versus multi-statement) plus the cursor position, keeping the upstream message as diagnostic detail only. Matching never depends on upstream prose; new failure shapes extend the closed set deliberately.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide the error vocabulary, or neither vocabulary keeps the required contracts.
criteria.verbatim_upstream: Surface the upstream message and character cursor position unchanged, mapping the cursor to manifest byte spans. Diagnostics quote PostgreSQL prose; I37 classifies by span presence rather than message text, and message wording may shift with parser upgrades.

error_vocabulary.instructions: Choose how the adapter surfaces upstream failures: verbatim message plus cursor, or a closed reason vocabulary with the message demoted to detail. Use common and topics.error_vocabulary.

criteria.bundled_call: Expose one adapter call per descriptor that runs upstream Parse and Scan together and returns statements, tokens, spans, and the error in a single compiler-owned struct. Callers cannot observe a parse without its scan.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide the call packaging, or neither packaging keeps the required contracts.
criteria.separate_calls: Expose Parse and Scan as independent adapter functions returning compiler-owned statement and token shapes. I37 invokes each once per descriptor and can test or reuse either pass alone.

result_packaging.instructions: Choose whether the adapter exposes one bundled parse+scan call or separate Parse and Scan entry points. Use common and topics.result_packaging.

fixed_constraints: P12 pins libpg_query for one PostgreSQL major and requires the actual parser plus scanner: one approved statement per descriptor, contiguous $1..$N application parameters, scanner byte offsets splitting static SQL into Bun tagged-template segments, and a top-level LIMIT as the distinct trailing parameter. No handwritten SQL lexer, parser, or query algorithm; no backend-specific AST across checker files; no fallback lexer when the scanner lacks data.

Both measured candidates embed PostgreSQL 17.7 (PG_VERSION_NUM 170007): pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2 dated 2026-01-28 with libpg_query 17-6.2.2, and go-pgquery v0.0.0-20260915022521-81f99195012b dated 2026-09-15 with wazero v1.12.0 and an embedded 2488452-byte WebAssembly module built from the same 17.7 sources. go-pgquery returns pg_query_go/v6 protobuf types.

Measured parity on a 24-case corpus (ordinary/repeated/multi-digit parameters, single/escape/dollar-quoted strings, line and nested block comments, multibyte UTF-8 before tokens, malformed grammar, unterminated strings, multi/empty/comment/semicolon-only inputs, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with and without RETURNING, subquery and literal LIMIT): raw parse and scan JSON, token spans, statement spans, parameter numbers and spans, and error message plus cursor match byte for byte. Only the Go error wrapper names differ (*parser.Error versus *pgerror.Error).

Measured cost on Apple M4 darwin/arm64: cold process parse+scan of the 105-byte P13 SELECT takes about 5 ms wall (1 ms inside) via CGo versus about 454 ms wall (447 ms inside, one-time wazero compile) via WASM. Warmed: parse about 14 us and 3.3 KB over 70 allocations (CGo) versus about 45 us and 85 KB over 78 allocations (WASM); scan about 2 us versus 5 us. Binaries: CGo 13461954 bytes; WASM 20639362 bytes, or 15403074 bytes with CGO_ENABLED=0. Cold builds from a fresh module cache take 6.7 s (CGo, needs clang) versus 7.4 s (WASM, pure Go). A 1200 parse+scan batch peaks near 12 MB RSS (CGo) versus near 300 MB transient RSS (WASM, 12 MB retained under GC pressure).

Release facts: distribution/build.go compiles the launcher with CGO_ENABLED=0 today; plan.md permits Go/C developer tooling for source builds keyed to the SQL binding choice while release users need no C compiler. CGo is the official pganalyze binding with tagged releases (BSD-3-Clause plus PostgreSQL License); WASM is a third-party binding with no tags (pseudo-version pin), MIT plus BSD NOTICE plus PostgreSQL-derived bytes plus Apache-2.0 wazero, and needs WebAssembly threads and exception handling, which wazero 1.12.0 provides. canlc parses each SQL descriptor at check time in short-lived batch processes.
common.purpose: Advise the Can compiler strictly from the evidence supplied here. Do not browse, implement, or explain. When candidates cannot be separated on the evidence, choose the marked uncertainty outcome.

binding_choice.facts: The compiler parses each SQL manifest descriptor once per check in a short-lived batch process; descriptor counts per project are in the tens. CGo keeps every canlc invocation fast and lean but requires clang plus CGO_ENABLED=1 wherever canlc itself is built, flipping the current CGO_ENABLED=0 launcher build. WASM keeps canlc builds pure Go but taxes every SQL-touching invocation with a one-time ~450 ms compile and ~300 MB transient peak, ships a larger binary, and pins an untagged third-party revision. Both expose identical parse trees, scanner tokens, byte spans, and error message/cursor positions.

error_vocabulary.facts: Both bindings report failures as message plus Cursorpos, a character offset into the statement, alongside source function, file, line, and optional context. Can diagnostics for manifests need byte spans into can.project.json statement text plus a stable classification I37 can match without string-sniffing upstream prose. Upstream messages change across libpg_query releases; cursor positions are stable for a fixed input and parser.

result_packaging.facts: libpg_query exposes parsing and scanning as separate entry points; each descriptor needs the statement list with spans from Parse and the token stream with spans from Scan. A bundled adapter call runs both behind one Go function and returns one struct; separate calls let I37 invoke each independently. Descriptors are validated once per compile; nothing re-parses at runtime.
